thread:
Tom (Acme): hey, support — over the last 24h we've been getting intermittent 429s from the API when targeting model r7-small. It only happens during our morning traffic spike and when we batch 10 user messages into a single call. No auth errors.

claire: sorry you're hitting that. can you paste the exact request payload and the 429 body you saw? also which region and api key (prod vs staging)?

Tom (Acme): prod key. region=us-west. example payload: ```{
  "model": "r7-small",
  "input": [ ... 10 items ... ],
  "max_tokens": 512
}``` response body: ```{
  "error": "rate_limit_exceeded",
  "message": "Per-model RPM exceeded: allowed 120 RPM for model r7-small"
}``` headers included: `x-rw-rpm-limit: 120`, `x-rw-tpm-limit: 10000`, `x-rw-concurrency-limit: 12`

jamal: thanks — a few things to flag: 1) per-model RPM/TPM limits are enforced separately from org-level quotas, 2) concurrent request caps are low on r7-small by design to protect latency, 3) batching multiplies token throughput and can spike TPM quickly. are you sending all 10 items in one request (single multi-input) or 10 parallel requests?

Tom (Acme): single request with array input. we do that to keep network overhead down. each item is ~1.2k tokens, so the total request can be ~12k tokens.

ashley: that explains it — TPM and contextual cost matter. when you send one huge request you hit the per-model TPM ceiling even if RPM is fine. also long-context requests can cause internal throttling because they occupy KV cache slots longer which reduces effective concurrency.

claire: can you repro quickly? two simple repro steps we use: 1) run a loop that calls the same payload every 5s for 3 minutes, 2) capture response headers and body. if you see `x-rw-tpm-remaining: 0` or `x-rw-rpm-remaining: 0` that's a clear quota exhaustion.

Tom (Acme): repro script (bash): ```for i in {1..36}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $PROD" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"r7-small","input":["..big..","..big..","..big.."]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate; sleep 5; done``` After ~10 iterations we see 429s.

jamal: good repro. couple of options: *reduce batch size* (split 10 -> 2–3 per call), *stagger* requests with jitter, or *switch to a model variant with higher TPM/concurrency* (r7-medium or dedicated capacity). For immediate mitigation set client backoff to exponential with jitter and treat 429 as retryable if you have non-idempotent semantics built in.

Tom (Acme): curious about context-length throttling — we have items that are long so the request length sometimes exceeds 16k tokens. Does that cause extra throttling beyond TPM/RPM?

ashley: yes — models with long-context support still have internal safeguards. Very long requests can be scheduled on slower execution paths (different kernel selection) or be refused if they push the runtime memory/cpu beyond per-node limits. In practice that looks like higher latency, occasional 503s or 429s flagged as `context_throttle`. If you can, trim context or switch to a variant with larger context or dedicated nodes.

claire: for debugging, please send one example request id (from response header `x-rw-request-id`) when you hit the 429 and we can pull the server-side logs. ops-bot, can you check logs for request id `req-6b1f9a` in us-west around ts 1775123500?

ops-bot: ack — pulling logs... found matching entries: \n```\n[1775123498] req-6b1f9a r7-small handle_request tokens_in=12200 tokens_out=480 duration_ms=1320 node=gw-3 cpu=78% cache_slots=3 result=rate_limit_exceeded\n```\n
jamal: looks like the request consumed a lot of KV/cache time (cache_slots=3) and kept a slot for 1.3s which reduces concurrent capacity. Combined with other users spiking, that pushes you over the per-model concurrency cap (12).

Tom (Acme): would using streaming help? we prefer getting whole result per user to keep ordering, but if streaming reduces the concurrency footprint maybe we can change.

ashley: streaming reduces memory pressure because tokens are flushed earlier, but it doesn't change TPM accounting at the platform-level. It can reduce peak latency and cache hold time, so it sometimes helps during bursts. Worth trying for the largest items.

claire: long-term fixes: 1) shard requests so each call stays well under the model's TPM limit, 2) evaluate r7-medium or r7-large for higher concurrency/TPM, 3) request a per-model quota increase if you need consistent throughput (we can fast-track for enterprise accounts), 4) consider Redwood Dedicated if you need predictable throughput and higher concurrent capacity.

Tom (Acme): can we get an immediate short-term config change? e.g., temp bump to per-model concurrency or a burst window?

claire: we can grant a temporary burst uplift for 2 hours from support console for your org, but that only helps if capacity is available. I filed a support action item: #SUP-2389 and requested `+50% burst uplift for r7-small in us-west` until 1775127200.

jamal: also patch your client: add `Retry-After` handling and jittered exponential backoff, lower batch size to 3, and instrument `x-rw-rpm-remaining`/`x-rw-tpm-remaining` in telemetry to alert before exhaustion. Example pseudo-backoff: ```sleep = base * 2**retries + rand(0, base)```

Tom (Acme): thanks all — we applied smaller batches and backoff and the 429s stopped during the next spike. we'll follow up if the uplift isn't sufficient. appreciate the quick assist. :thumbsup:

claire: glad that helped. leaving the thread open until uplift expires — if you still see errors after that send the `x-rw-request-id` and we'll escalate to infra.

Tom (Acme): will do. closing soon if nothing else.

ops-bot: (automated) support action SUP-2389 assigned to claire, status=active, expires=1775127200

claire: closing notes for internal record: cause = combined effect of large multi-input batches + per-model TPM + reduced effective concurrency due to long-context requests. mitigations = client batching change, exponential backoff, temporary burst uplift, recommend model variant or Dedicated for steady high throughput.

ashley: added an ops alert to watch r7-small tpm exhaustion for next 24h.

Tom (Acme): confirmed — all green this morning. thanks again!
